transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me?

Well... I didn't really want to come here. It's just... my family and friends. We keep fighting. 

They keep waving these bank papers at me, saying they prove nothing was taken. But... I know they're hiding my money. I've known for over a year now. They just... they use all these things to cover it up. Like bills, and fundraisers, and trip plans. 

I just... I have to keep confronting them. Until they finally tell the truth. That's all.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you don't seem to notice?
No. I don't... I don't hear things. Or see things. I'm not crazy. I just... I know what they're doing with my money. That's all.
Aside from these concerns about your money, how have things been going with your daily routine—like work, taking care of yourself, or your usual activities?

Things are... fine. Just the same as always. 

I mean, aside from the fights, nothing's really changed. I still make my own meals. I get myself to the clinic and my assistance appointments when I need to. I keep my things organized. 

I take care of myself. I'm fine.
Have you had any recent head injuries, seizures, or other medical or neurological problems, or used alcohol or drugs, around the time these beliefs about your money started?
No. I don't... I don't do drugs. Or drink. And I haven't hit my head or anything. I don't have any of those problems. I'm just telling you what's happening with my money.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre delusion (belief that family/friends are stealing money and fabricating cover stories) persisting for over a year. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech or behavior, and no other psychotic symptoms. Functioning outside the delusional belief system remains intact (self-care, appointments, daily routine preserved), and there is no evidence of mood episode, substance use, or medical/neurological cause. This presentation is most consistent with Delusional Disorder, persecutory type, rather than Schizophrenia (which requires broader symptom criteria and functional decline) or a mood disorder with psychotic features (no manic/depressive symptoms elicited).
